correction.text: Cieszyn and Bielsko, after Oświęcim split off c. 1315

keyframe_review.note: Oświęcim 'split off around 1315'; the remaining duchy became a Bohemian fief in 1327 and joined the Bohemian Crown in 1348.
Bielsko was split off (1572 in the infobox, 1560 in the body: Frederick Casimir died in 1571 and Bielsko was sold to the Princes of Pless).

region.text: Cieszyn with Oświęcim and the lands east of the Biała River, as the Duchy of Racibórz dossier names them

ledger.note: 1290: Mieszko founds the Duchy of Cieszyn. 'After another partition in 1290, Mieszko took his residence in Cieszyn'; Mieszko is listed as ruler 1290-1315; the page says the duchy was 'split off from Opole-Racibórz in 1281'.
c. 1315: 'Oświęcim split off around 1315' as its own duchy.
1572 (infobox) or 1560 (body): Bielsko is split off; 'Frederick Casimir died in 1571, and Bielsko was then sold to the Princes of Pless'. The two dates in the page differ.

1653: Elizabeth Lucretia dies and the duchy passes to the Bohemian monarchs, the Habsburgs; the male Piast line had ended with Frederick William in 1625 (the body also says Piast rule continued until 1653).
1722: Charles VI 'separated Teschen from the Bohemian Crown' and granted it to Leopold of Lorraine.
1766: 'Teschen passed to Francis' eldest surviving daughter' Maria Christina and her husband Albert of Saxony (Saxe-Teschen); in 1822 the duchy went to Archduke Charles.
1849: the duchy merges into the Austrian Silesia crown land (the body gives 1849, the lead says 'after the Revolutions of 1848'). The ducal title and the crown land were disestablished in 1918.
1849: the Duchy of Teschen ends as a territorial unit inside Austrian Silesia; in 1918-1920 its land is split along the Olza between Czechoslovakia and Poland.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; the duchy is known as Cieszyn Silesia, whose limit was later the Olza line of the 5 November 1918 agreement.

notes:
The Duchy of Cieszyn is a state Cliopatria lacks (eu-15-i and eu-15-e flagged it). One page only (budget 1-2): no area, no full ruler list, no wars. Bohemian suzerainty (1327 homage to John of Bohemia, 1348 incorporation into the Bohemian Crown) is the overlord's ledger: kingdom-of-bohemia should carry vassal_start (1327) naming duchy-of-cieszyn and its end in 1653/1722. The 1327 and 1348 events are therefore not in this ledger.

Not settled: (1) 1281 (page lead, the split from Opole-Racibórz) against 1290 (Mieszko in Cieszyn, the Racibórz dossier's loss): start 1290. (2) The ducal title and the 1918-1920 history (Olza line, 5 November 1918; Polish-Czechoslovak War from 23 January 1919; Spa 28 July 1920) are outside the 1849 end. (3) The Duchy of Oświęcim (c. 1315-1457) has its own dossier, duchy-of-oswiecim. (4) Bielsko 1560 against 1572. (5) The ruler list (Mieszko 1290-1315 only) is not given. (6) Radii are stand-ins.
